approachQuestion.prompt:
Check a relabeling agreement

Input: equally long arrays source and target of integer labels. Return true exactly when one consistent one-to-one relabeling turns source into target position by position. Every occurrence of a source label must use the same target label, and two different source labels must not share a target label. Labels absent from source impose no requirements.

Example 1: source = [4, 9, 4], target = [7, 2, 7]. Output: true. Example 2: source = [4, 9], target = [7, 7]. Output: false. Example 3: source = [], target = []. Output: true.

Constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 200,000; both arrays have length n. Labels are signed 32-bit integers. Do not mutate either input. Prefer the least expected growth in running time; among equally fast methods, avoid unnecessary asymptotic auxiliary storage. Assume non-adversarial integer hashing with expected amortized constant-cost operations.

options.text: Scan corresponding positions, checking a source-to-target map and a target-to-source map for conflicting bindings; then store both bindings.
options.feedback: Both checks are necessary: the forward map prevents inconsistent reuse, and the reverse map prevents distinct source labels from merging.

options.text: For each array separately, map every label to its first index. In one aligned scan, require the two current first indices to match.
options.feedback: Matching first-occurrence indices means exactly the same equality classes occupy the same positions, so it enforces the same one-to-one relation with equivalent resource growth.

options.text: Perform the same two-direction binding checks using balanced comparison-tree maps.
options.feedback: This enforces every binding correctly, but repeatedly orders keys when only direct lookup is needed.

options.text: Check and store only the source-to-target binding.
options.feedback: For source [4,9] and target [7,7], each source has a consistent target but the mapping is not one-to-one.

feedback.reason: Recognize that a one-to-one relation needs consistency in both directions.
details: Scan the two arrays together. Reject a position if either existing forward or reverse binding conflicts; otherwise store both bindings. Return true after the scan.
Forward consistency alone permits two source labels to share one destination. The reverse map rejects that collapse, enforcing a bijection on the labels actually observed.

“Scan corresponding positions, checking a source-to-target map and a target-to-source map for conflicting bindings; then store both bindings.”: Both checks are necessary: the forward map prevents inconsistent reuse, and the reverse map prevents distinct source labels from merging.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Check both binding directions”, n is the common array length and u is the number of distinct labels in source. Choose its time and auxiliary-space pair. Use the tightest standard bound for the worst legal input of size n, with expected time over non-adversarial hashing. Fixed-width integer and fixed-size tuple hash operations take expected amortized O(1); arithmetic, comparison and copying one integer take O(1). Auxiliary space excludes the supplied input and returned result, includes all maps, sets, temporary copies and call stacks. The method is iterative, with constant call-stack space.
constraints: Use the tightest standard bound for the worst legal input of size n, with expected time over non-adversarial hashing. Fixed-width integer and fixed-size tuple hash operations take expected amortized O(1); arithmetic, comparison and copying one integer take O(1). Auxiliary space excludes the supplied input and returned result, includes all maps, sets, temporary copies and call stacks. The method is iterative, with constant call-stack space.

options.text: Expected O(n + 1) time; O(u + 1) auxiliary space.
Guaranteed O(n + 1) time for every collision pattern; O(u + 1) space.

feedback.reason: Each aligned pair updates or checks two bounded-size map records.
details: Recognize that a one-to-one relation needs consistency in both directions.
Each of n positions uses a constant number of expected amortized constant-cost operations; empty input takes constant time. Hence expected O(n + 1).

At most one forward entry per source label and one reverse entry per used target label are retained. Before rejection there can be at most u + 1 such target labels, so O(u + 1) covers success, rejection and empty input. No input copies are made.
“Expected O(n + 1) time; O(u + 1) auxiliary space.”: Correct under the stated expected/amortized hashing model.
“Guaranteed O(n + 1) time for every collision pattern; O(u + 1) space.”: Ordinary hashing gives an expected bound, not a guarantee for every collision pattern.
“Expected O(n + 1) time; O(1) space.”: The two maps can retain u separate bindings.
“Expected O(n² + 1) time; O(u + 1) space.”: The method does not compare each position with every earlier position; a constant number of expected-cost lookups suffices.
